title: So, for Bellarmine, the will remains mistress of its act because the motion is in a way in its power
source_text: XV. Itaque ad argumentum, ex Bellarmini mente, dicendum est, quanquam Voluntas ad agendum egeat Dei motione praevia, & applicatione ad opus, illam tamen semper esse actus sui dominam; quia nimirum motionem illam quadantenus habet in sua potestate, qua ratione jam expositum est. Et quamvis posita Dei motione impossibile sit quin voluntas moveatur, voluntatem tamen semper in agendo liberam esse, quia fuit in ejus potestate a Deo non moveri; nempe se non disponendo per negativam illam determinationem ad motionem Dei recipiendam, quod erat penes voluntatem.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore to the argument, according to Bellarmine's mind, it must be said, that although the Will needs for acting the previous motion of God, and application to the work, yet it is always mistress of its act; because namely it has that motion in some measure in its power, in the manner already set forth. And although, the motion of God being posited it is impossible that the will not be moved, yet the will is always free in acting, because it was in its power not to be moved by God; namely by not disposing itself through that negative determination to receiving the motion of God, which lay with the will.
pass_b_english: On Bellarmine's view, then, the answer to the objection is this. Although the will needs God's prior motion and application in order to act, it is always mistress of its act, because it has that motion in its power to some degree, in the way just explained.

Once God's motion is given, the will cannot fail to be moved; yet it is always free in acting, because it was in its power not to be moved by God, namely by not disposing itself, through that negative determination, to receive his motion. That was up to the will.

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
